stories.summary: Citi analysts cut loan-growth forecasts to 6% from 6–7% for FY2027–28 and raised credit-cost assumptions, lowering estimates and target prices for DBS, OCBC and UOB, citing chip curbs, lower AI accelerator forecasts and asset-quality risks.
stories.title: Citi lowers Singapore banks' target prices on lower loan estimates, higher credit costs
stories.why: The call ties the US chip-export crackdown directly to Singapore's three banks, the backbone of the local market.

stories.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9–6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in its 2017 crackdown — the first time the court has found a state responsible for genocide — and ordered reparations and the safe return of refugees. Evidence pointed to about 10,000 killed.
stories.title: Rohingya: Historic International Court of Justice ruling finds Myanmar guilty of genocide
stories.why: A landmark verdict against an ASEAN neighbour, with implications for how states are judged under the Genocide Convention.

stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Health Sciences Authority announced tougher measures: repeat etomidate-vape offenders sent to the Drug Rehabilitation Centre a second time will serve double their previous stay, and under-16 repeat offenders must complete a 24-week intensive programme at IMH. Of 1,544 offenders caught between September 2025 and September 2026, 367 reoffended.
stories.title: Repeat Etomidate-Vape Offenders Face Double Rehab Stays on Second DRC Admission
stories.why: The vaping crackdown is escalating from fines to longer detention for repeat offenders, a significant policy shift.

stories.summary: One 97 Communications (Paytm) said its Paytm Singapore unit will invest up to 2 billion rupees (US$21.4 million) in affiliates of Singapore-based Funding Societies, with an initial about 1.6 billion rupees (US$17.4 million) for a 19.1% stake in CardUp, as part of a payments and technology partnership. The deal is expected to close by 20 May 2027.
stories.title: India's Paytm to invest $21.4m in Singapore's CardUp
stories.why: A cross-border fintech investment that deepens Singapore's role as a regional payments hub.

stories.summary: Anthropic shares began trading on Nasdaq, rising about 17% past the $83 allocation price to close at $97.17, after opening at $111.50 — making the Claude maker one of the world's most valuable public companies at about $1.76 trillion, despite the Nasdaq falling 2.3% the same day.
stories.title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
stories.why: The largest IPO on record is now a live public-market test of AI valuations — and it landed on a day the whole market fell.

stories.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia, probing whether the chipmaker's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information, following the scandal that ended CEO Jensen Huang's departure. Nvidia shares are down 22% since early November.
stories.title: California targets Nvidia in China AI chip probe
stories.why: A state-level probe adds a new legal front to the Nvidia–China story, on top of the House scrutiny already under way.

stories.summary: AMD shares fell 8% on Thursday after a report by short-seller Hunterbrook Media raised concerns that the chip company's firmware has been incorporated by IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker blacklisted by the US in March 2025, and by three linked server makers. AMD denies wrongdoing; Reuters could not independently verify the report.
stories.title: AMD shares slide as report says China links could invite US scrutiny
stories.why: AMD was seen as the safer AI-chip bet after Nvidia's troubles — this report argues it has its own China problem.

stories.summary: The Trump administration approved exports of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said — including 150,000 for Tencent, 75,000 for Alibaba, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD. Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million.
stories.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
stories.why: The most detailed public disclosure of AI-chip licensing ever, landing just as Washington tightens the rules further.

stories.summary: US stocks slumped on Thursday after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revitalise faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence. The Dow fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06 — its first close below 50,000 since June — while the S&P 500 lost 2.02% for a sixth straight session and the Nasdaq fell 2.25%.
stories.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI fervour
stories.why: Even the biggest IPO in history could not stop a broad sell-off; the S&P's six-day losing streak is its longest since April 2024.

stories.summary: Despite record AI-driven profits at Samsung and SK Hynix, foreign investors are selling Korean stocks for a seventh straight month in a 'Sell Korea' trend, with the KOSPI down 44% from its June record — though still up 20% year-to-date.
stories.title: Record profits but record outflows: 'Sell Korea' trade stalks Seoul market
stories.why: Record chip profits and record foreign selling at the same time — a striking split in Asia's biggest AI hardware market.

stories.summary: Gold is trading below $3,700 for the first time since September 2025, a little more than a third under the record near $5,600 it set in late January, as traders bet on more Federal Reserve rate increases. Silver has fallen far harder, from $121 to $44.
stories.title: Gold's 14-month low looks mild next to Silver's fall from $121 to $44
stories.why: The metals rout is the other side of the hawkish-Fed trade, and silver's collapse dwarfs gold's.

stories.summary: S&P/ASX 200 futures were down 1% on Friday morning, with the Australian dollar at its lowest since December 2025. The ASX 200 closed Thursday down 1.04% at 8,730.4, and December gold futures were down 2.12% at US$3,662.50 an ounce.
stories.title: ASX today, ASX 200 futures down 1%, S&P 500 down 2.02%
stories.why: The Wall Street sell-off and the commodity rout are spilling into Asia-Pacific markets this morning.

stories.summary: Ukraine's allies met on Thursday in Berlin for a Coalition of the Willing summit with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain, to stress wartime support for Kyiv and push for a European role in any future peace talks. More than 25 leaders attended, along with the heads of the EU and NATO and US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
stories.title: Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
stories.why: Europe's answer to the Shenzhen trilateral: a show of allied unity for Ukraine through its fifth winter of war.

stories.summary: President Donald Trump said on Thursday he would discuss renewed major strikes against Iran 'after the beginning of the year', pushing a decision he had previously suggested could come after this month's US midterm elections into next year. The US Senate again rejected a measure aimed at curbing the war.
stories.title: Trump Pushes Iran Strike Decision to Next Year: 'We've Got Time'
stories.why: The Iran decision is deferred, not dropped — and the joint statement after the Shenzhen summit did not mention the conflict at all.

stories.summary: The United States has signed a defence cooperation agreement with Venezuela just 10 months after capturing President Nicolas Maduro, restoring defence ties between Washington and Caracas after 21 years. The two countries intend to conduct joint military training, share intelligence and strengthen border security to combat drug trafficking.
stories.title: US restores defence ties with Venezuela after 21 years
stories.why: A remarkable reversal: Washington is now formally partnering militarily with the government that replaced Maduro.

stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time in a week, and said he was dropping any idea of a moratorium on attacking each other's energy sectors and shipping. 'I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge,' he said in Shenzhen.
stories.title: Putin threatens to hit back hard after third Ukrainian strike on Crimea bridge
stories.why: The bridge strikes have killed the one partial truce on the table — a halt to attacks at sea and on energy sites.

stories.summary: At the fourth India–Japan 2+2 foreign and defence ministerial meeting in Tokyo on Thursday, foreign minister S. Jaishankar flagged the 'weaponisation' of connectivity, resources and supply chains, while defence minister Rajnath Singh sought deeper cooperation in underwater and missile technology, as both sides reaffirmed a free, open, rules-based Indo-Pacific.
stories.title: 2+2 Tokyo dialogue: Jaishankar flags 'weaponisation' of resources; Rajnath seeks deeper cooperation in underwater, missile tech
stories.why: Two of Asia's biggest democracies are deepening defence tech ties, with supply-chain 'weaponisation' named as the shared threat.

stories.summary: The European Commission suffered a large-scale cyberattack involving an AI tool, ARTEX, used to identify vulnerabilities in its systems. Internal systems including the HR platform Sysper and medical reimbursement system MyPMO were disrupted for over 10 days, and employees' personal data may have been put at risk. The Commission confirmed the attack on 19 November and said it has found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole.
stories.title: Hackers attacked the European Commission using artificial intelligence – employees' data was put at risk
stories.why: The first confirmed AI-assisted cyberattack on the EU executive — and a warning that publicly available AI tools are now being weaponised against institutions.

stories.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard disclosed third-party cyberattacks, with Visa-related data released by a hacking group on 16 November suggesting several Asia-Pacific markets including Singapore were affected. JPMorgan said attackers had obtained some data.
stories.title: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard hit by third-party cyberattacks; Singapore among Asia-Pacific markets affected
stories.why: Three of the world's biggest financial names hit through third parties in one week — and Singapore is among the markets affected.

tldr: Singapore: Citi cuts target prices on DBS, OCBC and UOB as chip curbs and credit costs bite.
Technology: Anthropic closes its first day up 17% at $97.17, worth about $1.76 trillion.
Finance: Wall Street tumbles over 2% as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI fervour; the Dow falls below 50,000.
Defence: Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin as Putin vows a 'far more painful' response to the Crimea bridge strikes.
Information warfare: Hackers hit the European Commission with an AI-powered tool, knocking its HR systems offline for over 10 days.
